title: review follow-ups of PR #37986
body:
repo:objectstack#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibx7DSQZnugnuX8CpCM

Filing gate: ① (review follow-ups, one card per PR) · Source: fleet (L1 ACCEPT 7231247834 on PR #37986, Fixes #37435)

## What happens

PR #37986 (merged 9548be27) added the advisory lint rule `field/option-color-renders-neutral`, which warns when a select option's `color` is a value the badge renders as neutral grey. Its L1 review left these open:

- [ ] **A (L1 decision): define the nine option colour families once, in `@objectstack/spec`.** Today the list is written twice. The renderer has `BADGE_COLOR_MAP` at `ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx:1577`. The lint rule has `OPTION_COLOR_FAMILIES` at `packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts:1252`, and its docblock (`:1250`) asks that a new family be "added here in the same change". Export the family names from spec, and have both the badge renderer and the rule import them. `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/useRowColor.ts` keeps a third family-keyed map (`COLOR_TO_CLASS`, `:44`): read whether it should take the same list.
- [ ] **N1: the fix line for a family with stray whitespace names the wrong problem.** For `' red'`, `optionColorFix` (`data-model-rules.ts:1271`) says "Write the family in lowercase", but the trouble is the whitespace. The proposed fix, `color: 'red'`, is still right. Say "Remove the spaces" when `trimmed !== color`.

## Who meets it, and what it costs if not fixed

- An author who adds a tenth family to the badge palette must also find and edit the lint copy. If they miss it, every app author who uses the new family gets a false warning on `os validate` and save. The warning is advisory and never refuses, so nothing breaks, but authors learn to ignore the warning, and that warning is the only signal that a colour will render grey.
- N1 sends an author looking at letter case when the value is already lowercase.

## Done when

Each box above is fixed, or closed with a reason.

Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue BADGE_COLOR_MAP` → 3 hits (#37435 open, the source card; #36882 and #37406 closed), none on this mechanism. `is:issue "PR #37986"` → 3 hits (#37435 and two unrelated); no follow-ups card yet.
Reader: zone o3-ux of seat repo:objectstack#3 (or whichever lane triage routes a spec export to). The family export touches `packages/spec/src/**`, so triage should read whether it needs a contract review.
